geometry.derivationNote: The 11 October 1944 act admits the whole Tuvan People's Republic. Its production polygon is reconstructed as the Tuva-local component present in the independently verified 1945 USSR state and absent from the verified 1941 USSR state, with spatial controls around Kyzyl and neighboring non-Tuvan locations. This avoids silently substituting the modern Tuva Republic boundary.

territoryChanges.notes: Geometry-verified low/medium-resolution historical acquisition fragment; exact legal date remains 11 October 1944.

geometry.derivationNote: Source-verified internal union assignment of Tuva to the RSFSR. This does not create a second USSR external-boundary change. Any future historical Tuva AO polygon belongs to the internal-administrative visualization layer and is not required to mutate the sovereign territory replay.

geometry.derivationNote: The treaty entered into force on 5 February 1946. At that exact legal-effect date replay switches to the independently geometry-verified post-war USSR full state already corroborated by the treaty and 1945 historical cartography. This avoids approximating the complex Soviet-Polish line as a modern border trace.

territoryChanges.notes: Geometry-verified as a full-state replacement on treaty entry into force; detailed demarcation geometry remains a separate high-detail boundary dependency.

geometry.derivationNote: The later bilateral frontier-regime treaty identifies a signed authoritative package: descriptive frontier protocol, maps, and individual marker protocols with sketches/photos. It also states that the navigable Bug section follows the middle of the river. History Core records this as the exact geometry dependency; the package has not yet been transcribed into coordinate geometry.

The A2 Soviet act source-verifies the domestic legal/administrative treatment of South Sakhalin and the Kurils by extending Soviet nationalization to land and economic objects after the military events of 1945. It does not itself define a new external boundary, establish the de-facto-control transition, or settle international title, so it is documentary status metadata rather than a separate core-territory area mutation. The National Diet Library cartographic corpus remains useful evidence for a future source-backed reconstruction of the relevant islands on the appropriate control/legal tracks, but that geometry must be attached to the actual spatial transition rather than replaying the 2 February 1946 nationalization decree as an acquisition.

territoryChanges.notes: Domestic legal-status milestone only. De-facto control, external-boundary geometry and international treaty status remain separate spatial/evidence tracks.

geometry.derivationNote: Source-verified internal transfer of the 1954 Crimean Oblast from RSFSR to Ukrainian SSR. The USSR external boundary remains unchanged. The internal transfer can be visualized separately when a source-backed 1954 oblast polygon is available, but it must not mutate the USSR sovereign-territory replay.
